question: What is the primary function of a nursery in community health settings?

options.A: To provide permanent residential housing for orphaned infants
options.B: To serve as a center for early childhood care and public health monitoring
options.C: To act as a primary and secondary school for children above six
options.D: To function strictly as an isolation ward for infectious diseases

explanation: Nurseries provide out-of-home care while acting as vital contact points for public health interventions like immunization tracking and growth monitoring. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why are nurseries considered strategic locations for community health nursing interventions?

options.A: They gather many children and families in one place for easy health education
options.B: They guarantee that children will never contract infectious diseases
options.C: They operate independently of government health policies and regulations
options.D: They eliminate the need for routine home visits by community health workers

explanation: Gathering children in a structured facility allows health workers to reach larger populations of families simultaneously for program implementation. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which nursery type is typically established within an institution to support working staff?
explanation: Employer-sponsored nurseries are set up inside workplaces specifically to cater to the children of working employees. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: A nursery operated by a local government council in a rural area belongs to which category?
explanation: Facilities run by local government councils or NGOs to serve specific populations are generally classified as community-based nurseries. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: What fine motor skill typically develops between 6 and 12 months of age?
explanation: Infants develop the ability to pick up small objects using their thumb and index finger, known as the pincer grasp, during the latter half of their first year. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: A fifteen-month-old child in a nursery cannot yet walk independently or pull to stand. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Enroll the child in intensive vocational training classes immediately
options.B: Refer the child for a formal pediatric developmental assessment
options.C: Advise the parents to wait until the child turns three years old
options.D: Restrict the child from all physical activities in the nursery

explanation: Failing to walk by fifteen months falls outside the normal range for gross motor milestones and requires professional evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for regular surface disinfection in nursery facilities?

options.A: To eliminate the need for children to wash their hands
options.B: To prevent the rapid spread of infectious pathogens
options.C: To prevent electrical faults in play equipment
options.D: To improve the aesthetic appearance of plastic toys

explanation: Disinfection reduces the microbial load on environmental surfaces, stopping germs from passing easily among young children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why must handwashing stations be easily accessible within a nursery environment?

options.A: To ensure that toddlers can bathe independently every morning
options.B: To serve as decorative installations for visiting health inspectors
options.C: To replace the requirement for wearing protective gloves
options.D: To encourage proper hand hygiene before meals and after toileting

explanation: Handwashing is the single most effective way to interrupt the fecal-oral and contact transmission of infectious agents in group care settings. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: What type of feeding is recommended for infants during their first six months of life?
explanation: Global and national health guidelines recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life to provide optimal nutrition and immunity. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is food safety supervision critical in nursery meal preparation areas?

options.A: To eliminate the need for nutritional assessments in clinics
options.B: To ensure that children finish all food served on their plates
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing fresh ingredients
options.D: To prevent foodborne illness outbreaks among vulnerable children

explanation: Young children have developing immune systems that make them highly susceptible to severe complications from contaminated food and poor hygiene. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which transmission route is most common for gastrointestinal infections in nurseries?
explanation: Gastrointestinal pathogens typically spread when microscopic stool particles contaminate hands, surfaces, food, or water ingested by children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the most effective immediate nursing action when a child develops a rash and fever in a nursery?

options.A: Wait until the end of the week to see if the rash disappears
options.B: Encourage the child to continue playing with peers indoors
options.C: Administer leftover antibiotics from another child's bag
options.D: Isolate the child and notify the parents or health clinic

explanation: Isolating a potentially infectious child prevents further exposure within the facility while arranging for medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: What document should a community health nurse verify upon a child's admission to a nursery?
explanation: Checking the immunization card ensures the child has received age-appropriate vaccines to protect them and the community against preventable diseases. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h7)

question: A community health nurse notices several children presenting with watery diarrhea in a single nursery room. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Investigate the outbreak, enforce hygiene protocols, and report to health authorities
options.B: Close down the entire school permanently without informing the ministry
options.C: Ignore the cases assuming they are normal dietary reactions
options.D: Prescribe antidiarrheal medications to all children in the facility

explanation: An increase in similar symptoms signals a potential outbreak requiring immediate investigation, strict hygiene control, and public health reporting. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h7)
